label: Local source notes — curated from the cited primary source, not verbatim quotations. Follow the link to verify the exact wording.

0001.source: OWASP — Fail Open vs Fail Closed
0001.note: Fail-closed means a missing or unauthorised input leads to refusal, not a permissive default.

0002.note: State is the projection of an immutable event sequence; the events, not a mutable row, are the record.

0003.note: Permissions attach to roles and access is denied unless a role explicitly grants it.

0004.note: A subject sees only the tenant data and operations its role and scope permit.

0005.note: Secrets belong in a managed store with rotation and access control, never in source or plaintext config.

0006.note: An append-only log with chained hashes makes a tampered record detectable by replay.

0007.note: A trace id and parent id propagate across service calls so one operation can be reconstructed.

0008.source: Enterprise Integration Patterns — Dead Letter Channel
0008.note: Messages that cannot be delivered are routed to a dead-letter channel instead of being silently dropped.

0009.note: Retrieve relevant passages first, then condition generation on them; low confidence should escalate.

0010.note: No canonical primary source recorded. A weighted multi-KPI score is a local design choice, not a standard.

0011.note: Local-first keeps the working state on the user's device; the network enhances rather than owns it.

0012.note: Erlang C gives the probability a call waits, from offered load and agent count.

0013.note: Erlang B gives blocking probability where there is no queue — lost calls, not waiting calls.

0014.note: Service level is the share of contacts answered within a threshold such as 80% in 20 seconds.

0015.note: No canonical source recorded. FTE = required agents / (1 − shrinkage); the definition of shrinkage is local.

0016.note: No canonical source recorded. Adherence compares actual to scheduled interval behaviour; occupancy is handle time over available time.

0017.source: Practitioner knowledge — ICU/APU and the floor walker
0017.note: Known gap: no peer-reviewed source found during setup. Treat as practitioner practice, not a standard.

0018.note: CSAT measures perceived experience, FCR resolution without repeat contact, SLA/SL access speed. Practitioner definitions.

0019.note: Pydantic models validate at the boundary; FastAPI derives request handling and docs from those typed models.

0020.note: Streamlit reruns the script on interaction, so state that must persist has to be stored explicitly.

0021.note: Columnar Parquet for analytics, Postgres for transactional truth, Pandas for in-memory transforms.

0022.source: Docker Compose docs + CIS Docker Benchmark
0022.note: Compose defines local multi-container systems; hardening means non-root users, read-only mounts and no privileged mode.

0023.note: An SBOM lists what shipped; scanning fails the build on known vulnerabilities before release.

0024.source: Ollama / Piper TTS / Plotly / Tauri docs
0024.note: Local inference and local TTS keep prompts and audio on-device; the trade-off is hardware cost.
